selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main claim is made about the activity seen in the heavens?
questions.answer: It is presented as clear evidence that the Creator must exist and must be One.

questions.question: Which six features of heavenly rule are highlighted in the passage?
questions.answer: Bringing things under command, managing them, turning them, arranging them, purifying them, and assigning them duties.

questions.question: Why does the passage treat these features as proof instead of random events?
questions.answer: Because they appear on a vast scale, in a complete way, and can be directly observed in the heavens.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying this proof is even clearer than the heavens themselves?
questions.answer: The order and control shown in the heavens point so strongly to their Maker that the sign is more evident than the created things being looked at.

questions.question: How does the statement about the heavens connect unity with existence?
questions.answer: It teaches that the same heavens point not only to a real Creator, but also to the fact that this Creator has no partner.

questions.question: What role do all things in the heavens play in this testimony?
questions.answer: Everything in the heavens joins in showing the same truth, so the witness is broad and not limited to one part.

questions.question: What is the purpose of including the formal declaration after the explanation?
questions.answer: It sums up the meaning in a concise faith statement that turns observation into belief.

questions.question: How does the passage move from physical observation to a conclusion about Allah?
questions.answer: It starts with visible patterns in the heavens and then reasons that such perfect command must come from the Necessary Being.

questions.question: What does the phrase about observed perfection add to the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that the claim is not based on imagination but on things that can actually be seen.

questions.question: If a person accepted the greatness of the heavens but denied one Creator, which part of the passage would challenge that view most directly?
questions.answer: The part that says the same wide-reaching and unified control over all of them testifies to one necessary and unique Creator.

questions.question: According to the passage, what truth is found within the workings of the heavens?
questions.answer: A reality of complete control and wise management is found in them.

questions.question: Name two qualities of that reality that strengthen its force as evidence.
questions.answer: Its greatness and its all-embracing nature.

questions.question: What belief is supported by the witness of the heavens?
questions.answer: Belief that Allah necessarily exists and is One.

questions.question: Why is the testimony of the heavens described as something visible?
questions.answer: Because the signs of order and control are open to observation, not hidden from people.

questions.question: How does the passage treat the heavens: as silent objects or as witnesses?
questions.answer: As witnesses that point beyond themselves to their Creator.

questions.question: What does the phrase “Necessary Being” suggest in this passage?
questions.answer: It suggests a Being whose existence does not depend on anything else and cannot be absent.

questions.question: How does the passage show that the argument is about more than motion in space?
questions.answer: It includes not only movement, but also arrangement, purification, and purposeful assignment of roles.

questions.question: What kind of reasoning is being used when observed order leads to belief in one Creator?
questions.answer: It is reasoning from signs in creation to the truth about the One who made and governs it.

questions.question: Why would scattered or conflicting control weaken this argument?
questions.answer: Because the passage depends on the heavens showing one unified system rather than competing powers.

questions.question: What overall lesson should a student take from this short passage?
questions.answer: The heavens are not just beautiful to look at; their disciplined order teaches tawhid and points to Allah’s necessary existence.

questions.question: In simple terms, what is the passage asking the reader to notice in the heavens?
questions.answer: It asks the reader to notice the total order, control, and purpose in the heavens.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from that heavenly order?
questions.answer: That there is one Creator whose existence is necessary.

questions.question: Why are cleansing and assigning duties included along with movement and order?
questions.answer: Because the passage wants to show a complete system of rule, not just mechanical motion.

questions.question: What does it mean that the heavens testify “with all they contain”?
questions.answer: Every part of the heavens supports the same message, not only a few selected things.
